title: Colony and Protocol
premise: On the colony world of Vesper's Landing, Juniper Amberdale investigates impossible accidents while quietly maintaining a beacon whose original commission no record explains. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream of a burning ship, Juniper discovers the beacon is a receiver — and the dream is a message from the enemy fleet, offering terms of surrender that the colonial council intends to bury to justify a final strike. Juniper must smuggle the message through a colony sliding into martial law, betrayed by allies and hunted by her own employer, before the war ends not in peace but in extermination. In the end she delivers it at terrible personal cost, and the colony must choose justice outside the law over the corrupt order that kept them alive.
about_author: O. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. Halloran writes from a coastal town where the fog rolls in on schedule and every lighthouse has a story nobody will confirm.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Juniper Amberdale, POV. Investigating a cargo lift 'accident' that killed three dockworkers, Juniper notices the timing matches a pulse from the ridge beacon she alone maintains. She files her report omitting this detail. Emotional beat: quiet dread — the first hint that her private duty may be connected to the colony's misfortunes.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Night
chapters.summary: Dual POV: Juniper and schoolteacher Bram Okafor. Forty-one children wake screaming with the same dream: a burning ship, a voice counting down. The council dismisses it as mass hysteria; Bram doesn't. Emotional beat: creeping unease as the impossible becomes communal.

chapters.title: Terms in the Dark
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Decoding the beacon's dormant logs, she finds the dream's imagery matches an incoming transmission — surrender terms from the Ashfall Compact, the enemy everyone believed destroyed. Emotional beat: vertigo; the war's entire moral architecture begins to tilt.

chapters.title: Director Voss
chapters.summary: Council security director Voss, POV. Voss learns of the transmission and orders it classified, quietly arranging for the courier who carried it to have an 'accident.' Emotional beat: cold efficiency masking fear — power protecting itself.

chapters.title: An Impossible Accident
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. The courier dies in a sealed-atmosphere failure Juniper's own methods prove was engineered. Her investigation makes her a person of interest instead of an investigator. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The children's dream has evolved — now it includes a countdown and a map only Juniper can read. Bram brings this to her, crossing lines he can't uncross. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, two ordinary people conscripted by truth.

chapters.title: Martial Law
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Voss declares emergency protocols; curfews fall, comms are seized, and the council announces a 'final offensive' scheduled in nineteen days. Emotional beat: claustrophobia — the colony becoming a locked room.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: Juniper and Bram, alternating. Following the children's map, they find a pre-colonization vault beneath the beacon: proof the founders came here fleeing a war the Compact ended by mercy once before. Emotional beat: revelation — history rhyming, mercy forgotten.

chapters.title: Employer of Record
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Her insurance syndicate reveals it insured both sides of the war and ordered the beacon built as a back-channel — then sold out to the council's war faction. Emotional beat: betrayal; even the institutions of trust were arbitrage.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss discovers Juniper has the full message and sets a trap using her oldest friend, dockmaster Sefa Ilori. Emotional beat: the hunter's loneliness — Voss believes the lie is mercy.

chapters.title: Sefa's Choice
chapters.summary: Sefa, POV. Offered immunity to betray Juniper, Sefa instead burns her own clean record to buy Juniper a night's head start. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely given, the story's first pure act of justice.

chapters.title: The Long Ridge Road
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A night flight across the highlands with the message encoded in her beacon keys, pursued by drones, sheltered by farmers who ask no questions. Emotional beat: exhausted hope — strangers choosing decency at risk.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Dream
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Voss detains Bram and interrogates the children; one girl, Tally, recites the message verbatim, and its plain humanity cracks a young guard who lets Bram escape. Emotional beat: innocence as weapon, conscience as leak.

chapters.title: The Council of Nine
chapters.summary: Juniper, hidden, watches via stolen feeds as the council votes 6–3 to proceed with the strike and erase the Compact's offer from all records. Emotional beat: despair institutionalized — corruption wearing procedure's face.

chapters.title: Counterweight
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss finds the founders' vault evidence on her desk, anonymous. For the first time she hesitates, remembering her own family among the first colonists spared by Compact mercy. Emotional beat: the crack in the wall of power.

chapters.title: Broadcast Day
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. With nine days left, Juniper seizes the beacon array to transmit the message openly — but needs physical access through a garrison. Bram and the freed children create the diversion. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Tally's Countdown
chapters.summary: Tally, POV. Inside the garrison, the children hold the dream-countdown aloud in unison until soldiers refuse to fire on them. Emotional beat: moral collapse of the enforcers — you cannot shoot what you once were.

chapters.title: The Message
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At the array, wounded, Juniper broadcasts the Compact's terms and the founders' precedent to every screen on Vesper's Landing as Voss arrives with a gun. Emotional beat: climax — one small woman and one true sentence against the machinery of war.

chapters.title: Voss's Verdict
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Gun raised, Voss hears the broadcast name her own grandparents, spared by the last mercy. She lowers it and arrests the council's war faction instead. Emotional beat: redemption purchased late, justice finally wearing a lawful face.

chapters.title: Answer from Ashfall
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, brief. The Compact responds: ceasefire, negotiations, and a request to speak with 'the keeper of the beacon.' The colony exhales. Emotional beat: stunned relief, fragile as frost.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Funerals for Sefa and the fallen; Juniper declines honors, asking instead that the beacon's commission be written honestly into the record. Emotional beat: mourning without bitterness — survival's cost tallied and paid.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Light
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, coda. Months later, the beacon still turns, now officially maintained, officially remembered. Tally asks what it's for. Juniper answers: 'So the next message gets heard the first time.' Emotional beat: earned peace, vigilance kept as inheritance.
